# 47. Activity Definition vs Runtime Configuration

Do not read mutable Activity Definition fields as if they were the historical configuration of an already-running Activity.

Use:

```text
Activity Definition
= curriculum source

configuration_snapshot
= execution-time configuration
```

This preserves historic meaning.

---

# 48. Participant Role vs Platform Role

Do not conflate:

```text
participant_role
```

with:

```text
ADMIN / MASTER / MENTOR / STUDENT
```

Participant role is contextual to one Activity.

It must not grant global permissions.

---

# 49. Activity Input vs Copy

An Activity Input is a link.

Example:

```text
Activity B input
→ Development Object P123
```

not:

```text
clone P123
→ P456
```

unless later workflow explicitly requires a snapshot.

This preserves Project traceability.

---

# 50. Activity Output vs Artifact

M7 `activity_outputs` can point to Development Objects now.

M8 introduces Artifacts.

Do not model every Activity output as an Artifact prematurely.

Some Activities may produce:

- Development Object,
- Artifact,
- Decision,
- Evidence,

depending on the tool/workflow.

---

# 51. Completion vs Approval

Critical distinction:

```text
Activity Completed
≠
Artifact Approved
```

An Activity may finish its participant work while its output still requires:

- submission,
- review,
- revision,
- approval.

M8 implements those formal stages.

M7 must never mark an output approved solely because Activity status is completed.

---

# 52. Availability vs Authorization

Another critical distinction:

```text
Activity appears available
≠
user is authorized
```

The server must always re-check:

- user identity,
- Workspace,
- Project,
- Team,
- enrollment,
- dependencies.

Frontend display is advisory only.

---

# 53. Dependency Scope

Dependency evaluation should apply to the same relevant execution context.

Avoid accidentally satisfying a Team A dependency using:

- Team B's completed Activity,
- another student's Personal Activity,
- unrelated Project output,
- another Cohort's Activity.

The dependency source must match required Project/Workspace/Team/Cohort context.

---

# 54. Optional Inputs

Activity Definitions may support optional inputs.

Optional input absence must not block start/completion unless the Activity Definition's completion rule says otherwise.

Do not convert all input links into mandatory dependencies.

---

# 55. Required Inputs

Required inputs should be explicit.

If a required input is missing:

- start may be denied if dependency is precondition,
- or completion may be denied if workflow permits input collection after start.

Use the Activity Definition/configuration rule.

Do not invent one global behavior for every Activity if docs/config specify otherwise.

---

# 56. Instructor Case Study Activities

An Instructor Case Study should use the same Activity Engine.

Do not build a separate instructor-only Activity architecture.

Expected:

```text
CASE_STUDY Workspace
+
Instructor Case Study Project
+
same Activity Definition
+
Activity Instance
```

Student view/edit behavior follows Workspace/publication rules.

---

# 57. Workshop Reuse

The Workshop must use the same generic Activity Engine in simplified configuration.

Do not build a separate Workshop execution system.

This preserves:

```text
Workshop Project
→ Professional Course
```

continuity.

---

# 58. Cross-Program Reuse

Advanced Course Activities should later use the same M7 engine.

The Activity Engine must be curriculum-driven, not hard-wired to Professional Course session numbers.

---

# 59. Activity State Persistence

Canonical state must live in PostgreSQL.

Do not use:

- browser local state,
- transient realtime state,
- client cache,

as the source of truth for Activity completion, inputs, outputs, or participants.

---

# 60. RLS and Business Rules

RLS is defense-in-depth.

Some rules require server business logic, such as:

- dependency evaluation,
- completion rules,
- duplicate active-instance policy.

Do not attempt to encode every workflow rule only in RLS.

Required:

```text
SERVER BUSINESS OPERATION
+
RLS
```

---

# 61. Idempotency

Retry-prone operations should be safe.

Examples:

- start Activity,
- add input,
- add output,
- complete Activity.

Avoid:

- duplicate active Activity,
- duplicate input links,
- duplicate output links,
- multiple completion timestamps from retries.

---

# 62. Archive Behavior

Archived Activity Instance should remain historical.

Do not hard-delete:

- participants,
- inputs,
- outputs,
- completion data.

Archived Activity should not accept normal new mutations unless explicit restore/reactivation policy exists.

---

# 63. M7 Expected Repository Additions

Conceptually:

```text
features/
└── activities/
    ├── availability/
    ├── dependencies/
    ├── operations/
    ├── participants/
    ├── inputs/
    ├── outputs/
    └── validation/

lib/
├── permissions/
│   └── activity.ts
└── workflow/
    ├── dependencies.ts
    └── completion.ts

supabase/
├── migrations/
│   ├── ...activity_instances...
│   ├── ...activity_participants...
│   ├── ...activity_inputs...
│   ├── ...activity_outputs...
│   └── ...activity_rls...
└── tests/
    └── rls/
        └── activities...

tests/
├── unit/
│   ├── activity-availability/
│   └── dependencies/
├── integration/
│   └── activities/
└── e2e/
    └── activity-engine.spec.ts
```

Exact paths may vary.

---

# 64. M7 Completion Gate

M7 is complete only when:

```text
[ ] activity_instances exists
[ ] activity_participants exists
[ ] activity_inputs exists
[ ] activity_outputs exists

[ ] Activity Instance linked to Definition
[ ] Activity Instance linked to Cohort
[ ] Activity Instance linked to Project
[ ] Activity Instance linked to Workspace
[ ] Team link supported where applicable
[ ] configuration_snapshot stored

[ ] Activity availability resolver exists

[ ] completion dependency fully works
[ ] future dependency types do not auto-pass

[ ] startActivity() implemented
[ ] resumeActivity() implemented
[ ] completeActivity() implemented
[ ] addActivityInput() implemented
[ ] addActivityOutput() implemented

[ ] duplicate active Activity protected
[ ] participant identity cannot be spoofed
[ ] input source authorization enforced
[ ] output source authorization enforced

[ ] Team B cannot access Team A Activity
[ ] removed member cannot access Team Activity
[ ] Personal Activity private
[ ] direct ID access blocked
[ ] RLS tests pass

[ ] Activity completion does not imply Artifact approval

[ ] AT-ACT-001 PASS
[ ] AT-ACT-002 PASS
[ ] AT-ACT-003 PASS
[ ] AT-ACT-004 generic canonical-output handoff PASS
[ ] formal approval portion of AT-ACT-004 deferred to M8

[ ] lint passes
[ ] typecheck passes
[ ] unit tests pass
[ ] integration tests pass
[ ] E2E tests pass
[ ] RLS tests pass
[ ] build passes

[ ] no M8+ feature implemented prematurely
[ ] Codex reports READY FOR M8
```

Any dependency bypass is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

Any cross-Team/Personal Activity leak is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

---

# 65. Recommended Commit Sequence

Example:

```text
feat(activities): add Activity Instance schema
feat(activities): add Activity participants
feat(activities): add input/output links
feat(workflow): add Activity availability resolver
feat(workflow): add dependency evaluator
feat(activities): add start Activity operation
feat(activities): add resume Activity operation
feat(activities): add input/output operations
feat(activities): add complete Activity operation
feat(security): add Activity RLS
test(activities): add AT-ACT-001
test(workflow): add dependency enforcement
test(activities): add resume persistence coverage
test(activities): add downstream output reuse coverage
test(security): add Activity leakage tests
test(integrity): add configuration snapshot coverage
chore(security): complete M7 hardening
```

---

# 66. M7 Non-Goals

Do not accept these as "helpful additions" during M7:

- SCAMPER implementation,
- Brainstorm Entry implementation,
- Voting,
- Affinity,
- Mind Map,
- Artifact tables,
- Artifact Versions,
- Review/Approval system,
- Evidence,
- Patent records,
- AI Assistant,
- Sharing,
- File upload,
- Liveblocks,
- Daily video,
- advanced progress dashboards,
- hard-coded Professional Session logic.

---

# 67. Potential M7 Ambiguities Codex Must Flag

Do not silently decide if approved docs do not resolve:

- exact `participant_role` vocabulary,
- whether Team Activity auto-adds all Team members as participants,
- whether Master is auto-added as participant,
- whether Mentor is auto-added,
- exact duplicate/repeat Activity policy,
- whether completed Activity may be reopened,
- whether archived Activity may be restored,
- whether Activity can move back from completed to active,
- whether `submitted` state is used before M8,
- exact completion-rule DSL/format,
- exact `input_type` vocabulary,
- exact `output_type` vocabulary,
- whether Activity can consume input from a different Workspace in same Project,
- whether Personal Activity output can become Team Activity input before M13 Sharing,
- whether optional dependencies appear as warnings,
- whether Activity availability is time/release-date controlled,
- who may start Team Activity,
- whether Team Lead can start specific Activities,
- whether Master can start Activity on behalf of Team,
- whether Activity Instance is one per Team or one per participant for each method,
- whether completion is individual or collective for Team Activities,
- whether a participant may mark themselves completed independently,
- whether unfinished Activity survives Cohort completion.

If unresolved:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 68. Recommended Safe Defaults for Purely Technical Decisions

Only where they do not alter approved product policy:

- UUID Activity IDs,
- server-derived `started_by`,
- immutable configuration snapshot,
- canonical PostgreSQL state,
- RLS enabled,
- no cross-Team access,
- no cross-Personal access,
- one active execution per definition/project/workspace/team context unless configured otherwise,
- completion dependencies enforced now,
- unsupported future dependency types fail closed,
- future Artifact/Evidence/Decision foreign keys deferred,
- input/output links reference canonical objects,
- archive over hard delete,
- deterministic Activity test fixtures.

---

# 69. Review Checklist for Ahmad/FICI

Before implementation, confirm M7 reflects the intended Activity model:

```text
1. Curriculum Activity Definition and actual Activity execution are separate.

2. Every runtime Activity belongs to a real Project and Workspace.

3. Team Activities remain private to authorized Team scope.

4. Personal Activities remain private.

5. Activity participants cannot bypass Workspace/Project permissions.

6. Dependencies are checked on the server.

7. One Activity can require earlier completion/output.

8. The same Development Object should pass between Activities by reference.

9. Activity completion does not mean approval.

10. Formal Artifact/Version/Approval starts in M8.

11. Activity configuration is snapshotted at start.

12. The generic Activity Engine is reused by Workshop, Professional, Advanced, and future Programs.

13. M7 does not hard-code Professional Course-specific tools.
```

# FICI Invention Education & Development Platform
## Codex M8 Execution Prompts — Artifacts, Versioning, Review & Approval

**Document:** `22_CODEX_M8_PROMPTS.md`  
**Status:** Draft v0.1 — For Review  
**Depends on:** `01_PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` through `21_CODEX_M7_PROMPTS.md`  
**Purpose:** Provide exact copy/paste prompts for Codex to implement Milestone M8 safely and incrementally after M7 is complete.

---

# 1. Preconditions

Do not begin M8 until M7 is:

```text
IMPLEMENTED
→ TESTED
→ SECURITY-REVIEWED
→ COMMITTED
```

Required M7 state:

- Activity Instances exist,
- Activity Participants exist,
- Activity Inputs/Outputs exist,
- start/resume/complete Activity works,
- dependency engine works,
- Project/Workspace/Team scope is enforced,
- canonical Development Object handoff works,
- AT-ACT-001 passes,
- AT-ACT-002 passes,
- AT-ACT-003 passes,
- AT-ACT-004 generic handoff passes,
- Codex reports READY FOR M8.

If M7 is incomplete:

```text
STOP → FINISH M7 → REVIEW → COMMIT → BEGIN M8
```

M8 must not duplicate the Activity Engine.

---

# 2. M8 Goal

M8 creates the formal development-history mechanism for structured outputs.

The required lifecycle is:

```text
DRAFT
↓
SUBMITTED
↓
UNDER REVIEW
↓
REVISION REQUESTED
↓
NEW DRAFT VERSION
↓
RESUBMITTED
↓
APPROVED / CURRENT
↓
LATER SUPERSEDED BY A NEW APPROVED VERSION
```

The central rule is:

# APPROVED VERSIONS ARE IMMUTABLE

A revised artifact must create a new version.

Approved content must never be silently overwritten.

---

# 3. M8 Product Boundary

M8 includes:

- `artifacts`,
- `artifact_versions`,
- `artifact_object_links`,
- `feedback_items`,
- `submissions`,
- `review_actions`,
- `project_baseline_items`,
- Draft version creation,
- immutable version history,
- submission,
- review start,
- feedback,
- revision request,
- resubmission,
- approval,
- current-version pointer,
- supersession,
- reopen approved artifact,
- baseline foundation,
- Activity approved-output integration,
- RLS,
- approval transaction rollback,
- approval/revision concurrency protection.

M8 does **not** yet implement:

- SCAMPER-specific UI/data,
- Brainstorming-specific UI/data,
- Voting,
- Decision Records,
- Affinity,
- Mind Maps,
- Evidence,
- Patent Workspace,
- Sharing,
- AI,
- Files.

Those later milestones use the M8 Artifact system.

---

# 4. Artifact Principle

An Artifact is a higher-level structured project output.

Examples defined by the approved schema include:

```text
PROBLEM_BANK
SOLUTION_BANK
TEAM_DECISION_RECORD
INVENTION_STRUCTURE
GAP_LIST
MIND_MAP
INVENTION_CONCEPT
PATENT_LANDSCAPE
VALIDATION_PLAN
RISK_MAP
PRODUCT_ROADMAP
BUSINESS_CASE
MARKET_VALIDATION_MAP
TEAM_DEVELOPMENT_MAP
GTM_MAP
FINANCIAL_MAP
PITCH_PACKAGE
FUNDING_STRATEGY
```

Not every artifact type must have specialized UI in M8.

M8 implements the generic Artifact + Version + Review model.

---

# 5. Artifact Schema

Implement:

```text
artifacts
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `project_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `artifact_type`
- `title`
- `status`
- `current_version_id`
- `created_by`
- `activity_instance_id`
- `review_required`
- `approval_required`

Follow global metadata conventions where appropriate:

- `created_at`
- `updated_at`
- `archived_at`

Important:

`current_version_id` must point to the currently effective approved/current version where one exists.

Do not use `artifacts` row body as the versioned content store.

---

# 6. Artifact Version Schema

Implement:

```text
artifact_versions
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `artifact_id`
- `version_number`
- `version_label`
- `content_snapshot`
- `change_summary`
- `status`
- `created_by`
- `created_at`
- `previous_version_id`
- `approved_by` nullable
- `approved_at` nullable
- `approval_note` nullable

Approved statuses:

```text
DRAFT
SUBMITTED
UNDER_REVIEW
REVISION_REQUESTED
APPROVED
CURRENT
SUPERSEDED
ARCHIVED
```

Critical implementation rule:

# Version number is assigned server-side.

Clients must not choose arbitrary version numbers.

---

# 7. Approved Version Immutability

Once a version reaches approved/current state:

- content body is immutable,
- creator is immutable,
- version number is immutable,
- approval metadata is immutable except through controlled correction policy if later approved.

Do not allow:

```text
UPDATE artifact_versions
SET content_snapshot = ...
WHERE status IN ('APPROVED', 'CURRENT')
```

through ordinary application operations or user database credentials.

A change requires:

```text
reopen approved artifact
→ create new DRAFT version
→ edit new version
→ submit
→ review
→ approve
```

---

# 8. Artifact/Object Links

Implement:

```text
artifact_object_links
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `artifact_id`
- `artifact_version_id`
- `development_object_id`
- `role_in_artifact`
- `sequence`
- `metadata`

Purpose:

An Artifact version references stable Development Objects rather than duplicating them.

Example:

```text
Mind Map V2
├── System S1
├── Component C4
└── Gap G3
```

M8 must preserve both:

- artifact-level identity,
- Development Object identity.

---

# 9. Feedback Schema

Implement:

```text
feedback_items
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `project_id`
- `target_entity_type`
- `target_entity_id`
- `target_version_id` nullable
- `author_user_id`
- `feedback_type`
- `content`
- `status`
- `created_at`
- `resolved_at`

Feedback types:

```text
COMMENT
QUESTION
CORRECTION
SUGGESTION
REVISION_REQUEST
APPROVAL_NOTE
WARNING
```

Feedback must remain tied to the relevant version when it is version-specific.

Do not move old feedback onto a new revision silently.

---

# 10. Submission Schema

Implement:

```text
submissions
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `activity_instance_id`
- `artifact_id`
- `artifact_version_id`
- `submitted_by`
- `submitted_at`
- `status`
- `reviewer_user_id`

Statuses:

```text
SUBMITTED
UNDER_REVIEW
REVISION_REQUESTED
APPROVED
REJECTED
```

A Submission references one specific Artifact Version.

Do not submit a floating Artifact without a concrete version.

---

# 11. Review Action Schema

Implement:

```text
review_actions
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `submission_id`
- `reviewer_user_id`
- `action_type`
- `note`
- `created_at`

Actions:

```text
COMMENTED
REQUESTED_REVISION
APPROVED
REOPENED
REJECTED
```

Review actions form durable review history.

Do not overwrite previous Review Actions.

---

# 12. Project Baseline Schema

Implement:

```text
project_baseline_items
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `project_id`
- `baseline_type`
- `artifact_id`
- `artifact_version_id`
- `effective_from`
- `effective_to`
- `set_by`

Examples:

```text
CURRENT_INVENTION_CONCEPT
CURRENT_MIND_MAP
CURRENT_ARCHITECTURE_MAP
CURRENT_REQUIREMENTS
CURRENT_PRODUCT_ROADMAP
CURRENT_BUSINESS_CASE
```

The baseline must not be stored as one giant JSON document.

It is a collection of approved current references.

---

# 13. Baseline Policy — Important Open Question

The approved source documents explicitly leave open whether:

```text
artifact approval automatically updates project baseline
```

Therefore M8 must not silently decide this.

Safe implementation direction:

- implement `project_baseline_items`,
- implement explicit baseline update capability,
- make automatic baseline update configurable or disabled by default unless current approved docs define it,
- approval transaction may update baseline only if configured/approved.

If no policy exists:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

before hard-coding auto-baseline behavior.

---

# 14. Review Workflow Principle

Approved review lifecycle:

```text
Draft
↓
Submitted
↓
Under Review
↓
Revision Requested
↓
Revised
↓
Resubmitted
↓
Approved
```

Feedback remains tied to the relevant Artifact Version.

A revision request must not erase the submitted version.

```text
Artifact identity exists independently of Version content.
```

# 27. M8.11 — Approval Transaction

## Objective

Implement atomic formal Artifact approval.

## Approved Transaction

Must atomically:

```text
1. approve submitted version
2. supersede previous current version
3. update current pointer
4. update baseline if configured
5. close submission
6. audit
7. notify later/current minimal notification layer
```

```text
OBJECTIVE

INPUT

submissionId
approvalNote optional

AUTHORIZATION

Master / explicitly authorized approver in correct Project/Cohort/Team scope.

SERVER CHECKS

1. Submission exists.
2. Submission is in approvable state.
3. caller is authorized reviewer.
4. submitted Artifact Version exists.
5. submitted Version belongs to Submission Artifact.
6. required fields complete.
7. no competing terminal review state already committed.

TRANSACTION

1. identify prior artifact.current_version_id if any.
2. submitted Version → APPROVED/CURRENT according to schema strategy.
3. previous current Version → SUPERSEDED where applicable.
4. set approved_by.
5. set approved_at.
6. set approval_note.
7. artifact.current_version_id → approved Version.
8. update project_baseline_items ONLY if approved/configured baseline policy says so.
9. Submission → APPROVED.
10. create Review Action APPROVED.
11. create audit event.
12. create minimal notification side effect where available.

ATOMICITY

Every step succeeds or entire transaction rolls back.

NO PARTIAL APPROVAL.

IMMUTABILITY

After commit:
approved/current Version body is immutable.

TEST

- first approval
- second approval supersedes prior current
- Student approval denied
- unrelated Master denied
- stale submission denied
- artificial failure midway rolls back all state

VALIDATION

Run integration + transaction + RLS tests.

DEFINITION OF DONE

AT-REV-004, AT-REV-005 and AT-TX-001 pass.

FINAL REPORT

Return:
1. transaction algorithm

3. baseline behavior
4. rollback tests
5. authorization
6. results
7. assumptions
8. unresolved issues
```

# 39. Artifact Status vs Version Status

Do not conflate:

```text
Artifact.status
```

with:

```text
ArtifactVersion.status
```

Artifact represents the long-lived structured output.

Version status represents lifecycle of one specific snapshot.

If exact Artifact-level status semantics are not defined, keep them minimal and do not duplicate every Version state at Artifact level.

---

# 40. Current Version Semantics

The schema uses:

```text
artifacts.current_version_id
```

The approval contract implies this points to the currently approved/current Version.

Do not silently point it to every latest Draft unless an approved rule says so.

This distinction matters:

```text
latest draft
≠
current approved baseline
```

---

# 41. APPROVED vs CURRENT

The schema lists both:

```text
APPROVED
CURRENT
```

while the API contract says:

```text
submitted version → APPROVED/CURRENT
```

Codex must inspect current schema conventions before deciding whether:

- CURRENT is a separate status,
- APPROVED + artifact pointer implies current,
- approval performs APPROVED then CURRENT,
- only one current Version is enforced per Artifact.

If not already resolved in implementation docs:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

Do not invent contradictory status semantics.

---

# 42. Submission Identity

A Submission is immutable historical context for one review cycle.

If V1 is revision-requested and V2 is resubmitted, do not silently retarget old Submission from V1 to V2 unless the approved contract explicitly defines that behavior.

Preferred historical model:

```text
Submission S1 → V1
Submission S2 → V2
```

if consistent with implementation docs.

If current approved schema expects one Submission lifecycle object, flag and follow the source-of-truth decision.

---

# 43. Feedback Version Binding

Feedback should normally bind to:

```text
target entity
+
target version
```

when feedback concerns versioned content.

Example:

```text
"Component relation is unclear"
```

given on V1 must remain historically attached to V1 after V2 is created.

Do not silently move it to V2.

---

# 44. Revision Request vs Feedback

A revision request is both:

- a formal workflow transition,
- a review statement.

M8 should preserve:

```text
Review Action = REQUESTED_REVISION
```

and version-specific explanatory feedback/note.

Do not store the reason only in ephemeral UI state.

---

# 45. Rejection Policy

Schema supports:

```text
Submission status = REJECTED
Review Action = REJECTED
```

but the exact user workflow after rejection may be underdefined.

Do not invent whether rejection:

- permanently closes Artifact,
- allows reopen,
- requires new Artifact,
- permits new Version.

If needed:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 46. Withdrawal Policy

API includes:

```text
withdrawSubmission(submissionId)
```

but only:

```text
if review has not passed a policy-defined point
```

The policy-defined point is an open question.

Therefore do not implement broad withdrawal semantics without approval.

If no policy exists:

- preserve API placeholder,
- mark operation deferred,
- flag decision.

---

# 47. Review Authority

Review/Approval is not granted merely by role name.

Authorization requires:

```text
MASTER / authorized approver
+
correct Cohort/Project/Team scope
+
Submission assignment / reviewer scope
```

Do not implement:

```text
role = MASTER → approve any Artifact
```

---

# 48. Student Cannot Approve

This is a BLOCKER rule.

Even if a Student:

- owns the Artifact,
- created the Version,
- is Team Lead,
- submitted it,

they cannot call an approval endpoint requiring Master/authorized approver authority.

RLS and server authorization must both prevent escalation.

---

# 49. Team Lead Approval

Team Lead is not a Master.

Do not grant approval authority from `team_lead` membership role unless a future explicit workflow does so.

---

# 50. Artifact Version Content Storage

`content_snapshot` is the immutable snapshot of one Version.

Do not use it to replace canonical Development Objects.

An Artifact Version may contain:

- structured snapshot data,
- references,
- layout,
- presentation state,

while `artifact_object_links` connects canonical Project Objects.

This preserves reuse and history.

---

# 51. Version Source References

The API contract anticipates future:

- sourceDecisionIds,
- sourceEvidenceIds,
- sourceAiOutputIds.

Those entity systems are not all available in M8.

Do not invent them.

Preserve extension points and add actual source linkage when owning milestones are implemented.

---

# 52. Activity Completion vs Submission

M7 Activity completion and M8 Artifact submission are distinct.

Possible workflow:

```text
Activity work complete
↓
Artifact Draft exists
↓
Submit Artifact
↓
Review
```

or an Activity may remain submitted/review-oriented depending on its definition.

Do not globally equate:

```text
completeActivity()
=
submitArtifact()
```

unless configured.

---

# 53. Approval vs Decision

Formal Artifact approval is not the same as a Team Decision Record.

M10 creates formal human Decision entities.

Do not create fake Decision records during M8 approval.

An approval is a Review Action / Artifact lifecycle event.

---

# 54. Approval vs Evidence

Approval does not mean evidence is verified.

An Artifact can be approved as course/project output while containing items whose verification state differs.

Evidence verification belongs later.

---

# 55. Baseline vs Current Version

An Artifact may have a current approved Version without necessarily being part of the Project baseline.

Baseline inclusion is a separate Project-level selection.

Do not automatically equate all approved Artifacts with baseline items.

---

# 56. Baseline History

When baseline changes:

```text
old baseline item effective_to = timestamp
new baseline item effective_from = timestamp
```

Do not delete the old reference.

This preserves historical project state.

---

# 57. Archive Behavior

Artifact archive must preserve:

- all Versions,
- object links,
- submissions,
- feedback,
- review actions,
- approval history,
- baseline history references.

Archiving must not cascade-delete history.

---

# 58. Notification Scope

M8 workflows expect notifications for:

- submission,
- revision request,
- approval.

Full notification center belongs later.

Use the existing minimal notification foundation if present.

Do not build email infrastructure or notification-center UI unless already in scope.

If notification infrastructure is formally deferred, report only that side effect as deferred; do not pretend it passed.

---

# 59. Audit Events

M8 should record security/workflow audit events such as:

```text
ARTIFACT_SUBMITTED
REVIEW_STARTED
REVISION_REQUESTED
ARTIFACT_APPROVED
ARTIFACT_REOPENED
ARTIFACT_ARCHIVED
BASELINE_UPDATED
```

Exact event names may follow repository naming conventions.

Do not store full Artifact content in audit metadata.

---

# 60. Change Log Integration

Project `change_log` from M6 may record meaningful development changes such as:

- Artifact created,
- Version created,
- approved Version changed,
- baseline changed.

Audit log and Project Change Log remain distinct.

---

# 61. Transaction Requirements

The following must be transactional:

- Artifact + initial Version creation,
- Submission transition,
- revision-request transition,
- approval,
- baseline replacement,
- reopen approved Artifact where multiple writes occur.

Failure must not leave partial state.

---

# 62. Concurrency Requirements

Concurrency protection is mandatory for:

- version numbering,
- approval,
- revision request,
- current pointer updates,
- baseline replacement.

Forbidden outcome:

```text
two CURRENT versions
```

or:

```text
submission = APPROVED
but artifact.current_version_id still old
```

or:

```text
revision requested and approved simultaneously
```

---

# 65. Recommended Commit Sequence

Example:

```text

feat(versions): add immutable Artifact Versions

test(versions): add AT-VER suite

test(concurrency): add competing approval/revision
test(concurrency): add Draft conflict detection
test(e2e): add Artifact revision cycle
chore(security): complete M8 hardening
```

# 66. M8 Non-Goals

Do not accept these as "helpful additions" during M8:

- SCAMPER entries,
- Brainstorm entries,
- Dot Voting,
- Decision Records,
- Affinity groups,
- Mind Map editor,
- Liveblocks collaborative canvas,
- Evidence records,
- Patent records,
- AI outputs,
- Sharing,
- File storage,
- public publishing,
- advanced annotation engine,
- rich document editor,
- email notification infrastructure,
- automatic Project baseline mutation without approved policy.

---

# 67. Potential M8 Ambiguities Codex Must Flag

Do not silently decide if approved docs do not resolve:

- exact Artifact-level `status` vocabulary,
- exact semantics of APPROVED vs CURRENT Version status,
- whether `current_version_id` may ever point to Draft,
- whether Submission is one record per Version or reused across revisions,
- whether Student can withdraw before review,
- exact point after which withdrawal is forbidden,
- whether reviewer can reject Artifact,
- what rejection means for future revisions,
- whether Master may directly edit Team Artifact or only review/comment,
- whether one Artifact can have multiple simultaneous Draft Versions,
- whether multiple reviewers are allowed,
- whether Mentor may review or approve,
- whether Team Lead may submit,
- who may reopen approved Artifact,
- whether approval automatically updates baseline,
- which Artifact types map to which baseline types,
- whether all approved Artifacts become current automatically,
- whether version label is auto-generated or user-entered,
- whether DRAFT content is mutable in place before explicit checkpoint,
- whether every Draft save creates a new Version,
- autosave vs explicit Draft checkpoint behavior,
- whether approved Version can be administratively corrected,
- exact baseline replacement policy,
- whether archived Artifact may be restored.

If unresolved:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 68. Recommended Safe Defaults for Purely Technical Decisions

Only where they do not alter approved product policy:

- UUID Artifact/Version IDs,
- server-assigned version numbers,
- unique version number per Artifact,
- approved/current content immutable,
- revision creates a new Version,
- feedback remains version-bound,
- RLS on all review/version tables,
- direct client cannot mutate approval fields,
- approval uses one database transaction,
- one current pointer per Artifact,
- no hard delete of historical Versions,
- optimistic conflict detection for Draft writes,
- unique/locking protection against two current approvals,
- baseline history uses effective_from/effective_to,
- future Decision/Evidence/AI references deferred safely.

---

```text
12. Artifact current pointer updates only through authorized workflow.

13. Project baseline is a collection of current approved references.

14. Baseline auto-update must not be invented if policy is unresolved.

15. Approved output can now satisfy downstream Activity dependency.

16. M8 does not yet build SCAMPER, Brainstorming, Voting, Mind Map, Evidence, Patent, AI, or Sharing.
```

# FICI Invention Education & Development Platform
## Codex M9 Execution Prompts — SCAMPER, Brainstorming & Problem/Solution

**Document:** `23_CODEX_M9_PROMPTS.md`  
**Status:** Draft v0.1 — For Review  
**Depends on:** `01_PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` through `22_CODEX_M8_PROMPTS.md`  
**Purpose:** Provide exact copy/paste prompts for Codex to implement Milestone M9 safely and incrementally after M8 is complete.

---

# 1. Preconditions

Do not begin M9 until M8 is:

```text
IMPLEMENTED
→ TESTED
→ SECURITY-REVIEWED
→ COMMITTED
```

Required M8 state:

- Artifacts exist,
- immutable Artifact Versions exist,
- submission/review/revision/approval works,
- current-version handling works,
- approved versions are immutable,
- downstream approved-output dependency works,
- RLS for Artifacts/Versions works,
- AT-REV suite passes,
- AT-VER suite passes,
- approval transaction rollback passes,
- Codex reports READY FOR M9.

If M8 is incomplete:

```text
STOP → FINISH M8 → REVIEW → COMMIT → BEGIN M9
```

M9 must use the generic Activity Engine and Artifact system rather than creating a parallel workflow.

---

# 2. M9 Goal

M9 implements the first native FICI invention-method tools:

```text
SCAMPER
+
BRAINSTORMING
+
PROBLEM STORMING
+
PROBLEM BANK
+
SOLUTION BANK
+
PROMOTION TO STRUCTURED IDEA / PROBLEM / SOLUTION OBJECTS
```

The central product principles are:

# THINK PRIVATELY WHEN REQUIRED

# SHARE OR REVEAL INTENTIONALLY

# PROMOTE USEFUL OUTPUTS INTO THE PERSISTENT DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

# DO NOT LEAVE METHODOLOGY OUTPUTS AS DISCONNECTED TEXT

---

# 3. M9 Product Boundary

M9 includes:

- `scamper_entries`,
- `brainstorm_entries`,
- all seven SCAMPER lenses,
- SCAMPER create/update,
- SCAMPER → Idea promotion,
- Brainstorming create/update where appropriate,
- independent/private generation,
- reveal workflow,
- parent/extension relation,
- Brainstorm entry → Idea promotion,
- Problem Storming using Development Objects,
- Problem Bank Artifact,
- Solution Bank Artifact,
- Problem → multiple Solution relationships,
- Activity integration,
- Artifact integration,
- provenance,
- RLS/privacy,
- AT-SCAMPER acceptance tests,
- AT-BRAIN acceptance tests.

M9 does **not** yet implement:

- Dot Voting,
- Decision Records,
- Affinity grouping,
- Mind Map,
- Evidence,
- Patent tools,
- AI,
- general cross-Team sharing,
- generic Personal → Team sharing framework,
- Liveblocks collaborative board.

Those belong to later milestones.

---

# 4. Important M9/M13 Boundary

The M9 implementation plan mentions:

```text
personal-to-team sharing integration later via M13
```

Therefore M9 must distinguish:

## Activity-internal reveal

A Brainstorming Activity may intentionally support:

```text
private generation
→ authorized reveal
→ shared activity pool
```

This is M9.

## General entity sharing

A user selects a private SCAMPER/Artifact/Object and shares it across Workspaces/Teams using persistent sharing records.

This is M13.

Do not build M13 general sharing early.

---

# 5. SCAMPER Schema

Implement:

```text
scamper_entries
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `activity_instance_id`
- `project_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `created_by`
- `scamper_type`
- `original_element`
- `proposed_change`
- `result_text`
- `idea_object_id` nullable
- `status`

Approved SCAMPER types:

```text
SUBSTITUTE
COMBINE
ADAPT
MODIFY
PUT_TO_ANOTHER_USE
ELIMINATE
REVERSE_REARRANGE
```

The seven lenses must not be renamed or merged.

---

# 6. FICI SCAMPER Method

The Professional Course presents SCAMPER as a structured way to examine an existing product, component, function, process, system, or solution.

The FICI approach emphasizes:

```text
See
→ Analyze
→ Break Down
→ Understand
→ Apply
```

and all seven lenses:

```text
S — Substitute
C — Combine
A — Adapt
M — Modify
P — Put to Another Use
E — Eliminate
R — Reverse / Rearrange
```

The platform should support this methodology directly rather than reducing SCAMPER to one generic text box.

---

# 7. SCAMPER Entry Principle

Each entry records:

```text
lens
+
original element
+
proposed change
+
result
```

This supports traceability from:

```text
Original Concept
→ SCAMPER Lens
→ Proposed Change
→ Resulting Idea
→ optional Idea Development Object
```

---

# 8. Brainstorm Entry Schema

Implement:

```text
brainstorm_entries
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `activity_instance_id`
- `project_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `created_by`
- `content`
- `status`
- `revealed_at` nullable
- `development_object_id` nullable
- `parent_entry_id` nullable

This schema supports:

```text
private creation
→ reveal
→ promotion into structured Idea
```

---

# 9. Brainstorming Product Principle

The platform must support independent generation before group influence where the Activity Definition requires it.

Conceptually:

```text
A1 writes private ideas
A2 writes private ideas
A3 writes private ideas
↓
AUTHORIZED REVEAL
↓
shared pool
↓
build / extend / combine
↓
promote selected entries to Ideas / Solutions
```

Before reveal:

```text
A1 cannot read A2's unrevealed entries
A2 cannot read A1's unrevealed entries
```

This is a BLOCKER privacy rule.

---

# 10. Parent / Extension Relation

`brainstorm_entries.parent_entry_id` supports extending another Brainstorm entry.

Examples:

```text
Idea A
└── Build-on A1
    └── Build-on A2
```

The parent relation must remain inside the same authorized Activity scope.

Do not allow Team B entry to point to Team A entry.

---

# 11. Problem Storming Curriculum Principle

Professional Course Session 4 explicitly delays solving and explores problems from multiple perspectives.

Supported perspectives/categories include:

- User,
- Function,
- Technical,
- Cost,
- Safety,
- Environment,
- Accessibility,
- Maintenance.

Core pattern:

```text
Identify
→ Write
→ Keep Going
```

not:

```text
Identify
→ Solve
→ Stop
```

The output is:

```text
Problem Bank
```

---

# 12. From Problems to Solutions

The approved Session 4 workflow is:

```text
Concept V2
→ Problem Storming
→ Problem Bank
→ Brainstorming
→ Solution Bank
```

For each selected Problem:

```text
Problem
→ Solution A
→ Solution B
→ Solution C
→ ...
```

During generation:

```text
NO RANKING
NO VOTING
NO ELIMINATION
```

Evaluation happens in Session 5.

M9 must not embed M10 voting logic.

---

# 13. Problem Bank Architecture

Problem Bank must use:

```text
Development Objects of type PROBLEM
+
Artifact of type PROBLEM_BANK
+
Artifact/Object Links
```

Do not create a disconnected `problem_bank_items` text table unless source docs explicitly require it.

Each Problem should have a stable Development Object ID.

Problem-specific typed data may use the existing `problem_details` extension from M6.

---

# 14. Solution Bank Architecture

Solution Bank must use:

```text
Development Objects of type SOLUTION
+
Artifact of type SOLUTION_BANK
+
Artifact/Object Links
```

A Solution should be connected to its relevant Problem through explicit Development Object Relationships.

Use the approved relationship semantics.

Do not store only a flat list of solution text if structured Objects already exist.

---

# 15. Brainstorm → Idea Promotion

Approved operation:

```text
promoteBrainstormEntryToIdea(input)
```

Creates an Idea Development Object with provenance back to the Brainstorm entry.

Required behavior:

```text
Brainstorm Entry
→ Idea Development Object
```

The original Brainstorm entry remains.

Promotion must not erase source history.

---

# 16. SCAMPER → Idea Promotion

Approved API output allows:

```text
SCAMPER Entry + optional linked Idea object
```

Therefore the platform should support promotion from a SCAMPER entry to an Idea Development Object.

Required traceability:

```text
SCAMPER Entry
→ Idea Object
```

using:

- `idea_object_id`,
- origin/provenance metadata,
- Project/Workspace scope.

---

# 17. Private SCAMPER Rule

A SCAMPER entry created in Personal Workspace remains private unless:

- it is created directly inside an authorized Team Activity/Team Workspace,
- or later explicitly shared/promoted according to approved sharing workflow.

M9 must not infer that enrollment/team membership automatically exposes Personal SCAMPER work.

---

# 18. SCAMPER Share-to-Team Contract Boundary

The API defines:

```text
shareScamperEntryToTeam(input)
```

and says:

```text
Uses standard sharing/promote logic.
```

However the general sharing system is scheduled for M13.

Therefore in M9:

- do not invent a second ad hoc sharing model,
- implement only if the approved project already has the standard sharing primitive,
- otherwise keep the operation adapter/interface ready and mark full persistence as dependent on M13,
- AT-SCAMPER-003 may be implemented through a safe explicit promotion/copy mechanism only if the approved docs define it.

Do not silently expose the source Personal Workspace.

---

# 19. Brainstorm Reveal vs General Sharing

`revealBrainstormEntries()` is Activity-local and can be implemented now.

It is not equivalent to general `shareEntity()`.

Reveal means:

```text
entry belongs to this Brainstorming Activity
+
entry state changes from hidden/private-within-activity
to visible to authorized activity participants
```

It does not transfer ownership.

It does not grant access outside the Activity/Team scope.

```text
- AT-SCAMPER-002 PASS
- AT-SCAMPER-003 PASS or explicitly correct M13 dependency
- AT-BRAIN-001 PASS
- AT-BRAIN-002 PASS
- AT-BRAIN-003 PASS
- AT-BRAIN-004 PASS
- Professional Session 4 integration PASS
- zero known hidden-entry leak
- zero known cross-Team leak
- no M10+ scope creep

FINAL REPORT

Return:
1. security review
2. integrity review
3. issues found
4. issues fixed
5. remaining issues
6. BLOCKER status
7. test results
8. recommendation: READY FOR M10 or NOT READY FOR M10
```

---

# 43. SCAMPER Entry vs Idea Object

Do not conflate:

```text
SCAMPER Entry
```

with:

```text
IDEA Development Object
```

The SCAMPER Entry records methodology-specific reasoning.

The Idea Object records persistent Project content.

One SCAMPER Entry may optionally create/link an Idea.

The source SCAMPER Entry remains for provenance.

---

# 44. Brainstorm Entry vs Idea/Solution Object

Likewise:

```text
Brainstorm Entry
```

is not automatically a canonical Idea/Solution.

A Brainstorm Activity may produce many transient/raw entries.

Selected entries can be explicitly promoted.

This avoids turning every rough thought into permanent Project structure.

---

# 45. Problem vs Brainstorm Entry

Problem Storming should create structured PROBLEM Development Objects where the workflow intends persistent Problem Bank output.

Do not treat every Problem merely as a generic Brainstorm entry if it is meant to persist into later Sessions.

---

# 46. Solution vs Brainstorm Entry

Brainstorm entries may be the raw generation layer.

Promoted Solutions become:

```text
Development Object type SOLUTION
```

and can be linked to Problems, Artifacts and later Voting.

---

# 47. No Early Evaluation

Session 4 explicitly separates divergence from evaluation.

M9 must not add:

- score,
- rank,
- winner,
- top idea,
- accepted solution,
- vote count,

as automatic generation behavior.

M10 owns convergence and decisions.

---

# 48. Problem Categories

The course explicitly uses perspectives including:

- User,
- Function,
- Technical,
- Cost,
- Safety,
- Environment,
- Accessibility,
- Maintenance.

Map these to existing `problem_details.problem_category` values where the schema supports them.

Do not silently invent incompatible alternate labels.

If exact `functional` vs `function` naming differs in schema, preserve database vocabulary while keeping course labels visible at the product layer.

---

# 49. SCAMPER Lens Labels

Database values may use:

```text
PUT_TO_ANOTHER_USE
REVERSE_REARRANGE
```

while curriculum presentation may show:

```text
Put to Another Use
Reverse / Rearrange
```

Preserve the exact curriculum-facing wording without changing stable enum codes.

---

# 50. Editable States

SCAMPER/Brainstorm entries should only be editable while their Activity/workflow state allows editing.

Do not permit a raw-entry update to mutate an approved Artifact Version that references/promotes the entry.

Canonical promoted Project Objects and approved Artifacts have their own workflows.

---

# 51. Provenance

Promotion should preserve:

```text
source method
source Activity Instance
source entry ID
creator
Workspace
Project
timestamp
```

This is required so later AI/review systems can distinguish:

```text
raw brainstorm idea
vs
structured Project Idea
```

---

# 52. Reveal Is Not Approval

A revealed Brainstorm entry is merely visible to the Activity pool.

It is not:

- accepted,
- selected,
- approved,
- voted winner,
- Project baseline.

Do not change acceptance state merely because reveal occurred.

---

# 53. Promotion Is Not Approval

Promoting an entry to an Idea/Solution means:

```text
save as structured Project content
```

It does not mean:

```text
human team approved this as final direction
```

M10 Decisions and M8 Artifact approval remain separate.

---

# 54. Problem Bank / Solution Bank Versioning

Problem Bank and Solution Bank use M8 Artifact Versioning.

Therefore:

- bank content can be revised,
- prior versions remain,
- approved versions immutable,
- later Sessions can request approved/current Bank output,
- Development Objects remain stable across Bank versions.

---

# 55. Reuse Across Sessions

A Problem in Problem Bank V1 should be referenceable later by:

- Voting,
- Affinity,
- Mind Map,
- AI,
- Patent analysis.

Do not duplicate it when another tool uses it.

Likewise Solution Objects should retain stable IDs.

---

# 56. Same Project / Workspace Rules

All M9 records must bind correctly to:

```text
Activity Instance
Project
Workspace
Team if applicable
```

Do not allow mismatched foreign IDs submitted by clients.

Derive context from Activity where possible.

---

# 57. Activity Configuration Drives Privacy

Not every Brainstorming Activity must use hidden-before-reveal.

The Activity Definition/configuration determines behavior.

M9 engine must support:

- private-before-reveal,
- directly shared/team-visible generation,

if both are approved configurations.

Do not hard-code one mode globally.

---

# 58. Reveal Authority

Reveal authority should come from Activity configuration/policy.

Possible actors may include:

- Master,
- Activity host,
- Team workflow role.

Do not assume Team Lead reveal power unless approved.

---

# 59. SCAMPER Personal → Team Future Flow

The intended future flow can be:

```text
Personal SCAMPER Entry
↓
explicit share/promote
↓
Team can access selected entry/output
↓
creator remains recorded
```

M9 must preserve compatibility with this without exposing the entire Personal Workspace.

---

# 60. M9 Expected Repository Additions

Conceptually:

```text
features/
├── scamper/
│   ├── operations/
│   ├── promotion/
│   ├── access/
│   └── validation/
├── brainstorming/
│   ├── operations/
│   ├── reveal/
│   ├── promotion/
│   └── access/
└── problem-solution/
    ├── problem-storming/
    ├── problem-bank/
    ├── solution-generation/
    └── solution-bank/

lib/
├── permissions/
│   ├── scamper.ts
│   └── brainstorming.ts
└── provenance/

supabase/
├── migrations/
│   ├── ...scamper_entries...
│   ├── ...brainstorm_entries...
│   └── ...m9_rls...
└── tests/
    └── rls/
        ├── scamper...
        └── brainstorming...

tests/
├── unit/
│   ├── scamper/
│   ├── brainstorming/
│   └── problem-solution/
├── integration/
│   ├── scamper/
│   ├── brainstorming/
│   └── session4/
└── e2e/
    └── professional-session4.spec.ts
```

Exact paths may vary.

---

# 61. M9 Completion Gate

M9 is complete only when:

```text
[ ] scamper_entries exists
[ ] all seven SCAMPER lenses supported
[ ] createScamperEntry() implemented
[ ] updateScamperEntry() implemented
[ ] SCAMPER → Idea promotion implemented

[ ] Personal SCAMPER privacy enforced
[ ] exact SCAMPER ID cannot bypass privacy

[ ] brainstorm_entries exists
[ ] createBrainstormEntry() implemented
[ ] private-before-reveal mode works
[ ] revealBrainstormEntries() implemented
[ ] promoteBrainstormEntryToIdea() implemented
[ ] parent/extension relation works safely

[ ] unrevealed peer entries hidden
[ ] direct DB hidden-entry access blocked
[ ] revealed pool visible only to authorized Activity scope

[ ] Problem Storming creates PROBLEM Objects
[ ] problem_details used where applicable
[ ] Problem Bank Artifact implemented
[ ] Problem Bank uses stable Problem Objects

[ ] Solution generation creates SOLUTION Objects
[ ] Solutions relate to Problems
[ ] Solution Bank Artifact implemented
[ ] Solution Bank uses stable Solution Objects

[ ] no automatic ranking/voting/selection
[ ] methodology outputs registered with Activity Engine
[ ] Artifact Versioning used for Banks
[ ] provenance retained through promotion

[ ] AT-SCAMPER-001 PASS
[ ] AT-SCAMPER-002 PASS
[ ] AT-SCAMPER-003 PASS or explicitly valid M13 deferral

[ ] AT-BRAIN-001 PASS
[ ] AT-BRAIN-002 PASS
[ ] AT-BRAIN-003 PASS
[ ] AT-BRAIN-004 PASS

[ ] Professional Session 4 integration PASS

[ ] lint passes
[ ] typecheck passes
[ ] unit tests pass
[ ] integration tests pass
[ ] E2E tests pass
[ ] RLS tests pass
[ ] build passes

[ ] no M10+ feature implemented prematurely
[ ] Codex reports READY FOR M10
```

Any premature reveal is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

Any Personal Workspace methodology leak is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

---

# 62. Recommended Commit Sequence

Example:

```text
feat(scamper): add SCAMPER schema and seven lenses
feat(scamper): add create/update operations
feat(scamper): add Idea promotion
feat(brainstorm): add Brainstorm entry schema
feat(brainstorm): add private generation
feat(brainstorm): add reveal workflow
feat(brainstorm): add Idea promotion
feat(problem): add Problem Storming workflow
feat(artifacts): add Problem Bank integration
feat(solution): add Solution generation and relationships
feat(artifacts): add Solution Bank integration
feat(activities): integrate M9 methodology outputs
feat(security): add SCAMPER/Brainstorm RLS
test(scamper): add AT-SCAMPER suite
test(brainstorm): add AT-BRAIN suite
test(session4): add Professional Session 4 flow
test(security): add M9 leakage coverage
chore(security): complete M9 hardening
```

---

# 63. M9 Non-Goals

Do not accept these as "helpful additions" during M9:

- Dot Voting,
- Fist to Five,
- Planning Poker,
- Decision Records,
- Affinity groups,
- Mind Map,
- Evidence records,
- Patent search,
- Patent comparison,
- AI Assistant,
- generic Sharing records,
- cross-Team share UI,
- Liveblocks canvas,
- automatic ranking,
- automatic winner selection,
- automatic idea rejection.

---

# 64. Potential M9 Ambiguities Codex Must Flag

Do not silently decide if approved docs do not resolve:

- exact SCAMPER entry `status` vocabulary,
- whether every SCAMPER entry automatically creates an Idea Object,
- whether Idea promotion is one-click or requires confirmation,
- whether promoted Idea inherits creator or promoting user,
- whether private Brainstorm entries are visible to Master before reveal,
- whether Master can reveal all entries,
- whether Team Lead can reveal,
- whether participants can reveal their own entries individually,
- whether reveal can be reversed,
- whether revealed entries can be edited afterward,
- exact `visibilityState` vocabulary,
- whether Brainstorm entry can be promoted before reveal,
- whether private Brainstorm promotion should create Personal Idea or Team Idea,
- whether Problem Storming uses Brainstorm Entry records or directly creates Problems,
- whether every identified Problem must enter Problem Bank automatically,
- whether every promoted Solution must enter Solution Bank automatically,
- whether Solution → Problem relationship direction is exactly `SOLUTION SOLVES PROBLEM`,
- whether one Solution can solve multiple Problems,
- whether Problem Bank/Solution Bank are one Artifact per Activity, Session, Team, or Project,
- whether Bank Artifact approval is mandatory for Session 5 dependency,
- how AT-SCAMPER-003 should be satisfied before M13 standard Sharing exists.

If unresolved:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 65. Recommended Safe Defaults for Purely Technical Decisions

Only where they do not alter approved product policy:

- UUID SCAMPER/Brainstorm Entry IDs,
- creator server-derived,
- strict seven-lens enum,
- private-before-reveal fails closed,
- direct peer queries filtered by RLS,
- reveal timestamp immutable after reveal,
- promotion creates stable Development Object and retains source Entry,
- duplicate promotion prevented,
- Problem/Solution stored as Development Objects,
- Bank outputs stored as M8 Artifacts,
- canonical IDs reused across Sessions,
- no ranking or voting in M9,
- general sharing deferred to M13.

---

Before implementation, confirm M9 reflects the intended methodology:


# FICI Invention Education & Development Platform
## Codex M10 Execution Prompts — Voting & Decision Records

**Document:** `24_CODEX_M10_PROMPTS.md`  
**Status:** Draft v0.1 — For Review  
**Depends on:** `01_PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` through `23_CODEX_M9_PROMPTS.md`  
**Purpose:** Provide exact copy/paste prompts for Codex to implement Milestone M10 safely and incrementally after M9 is complete.

---

# 1. Preconditions

Do not begin M10 until M9 is:

```text
IMPLEMENTED
→ TESTED
→ SECURITY-REVIEWED
→ COMMITTED
```

Required M9 state:

- SCAMPER works,
- Brainstorming works,
- private-before-reveal works,
- Problem Storming works,
- Problem Bank exists,
- Solution Bank exists,
- Problems/Solutions are stable Development Objects,
- Problem/Solution relationships exist,
- M9 RLS/privacy tests pass,
- AT-SCAMPER tests pass or any M13-dependent share sub-case is explicitly deferred,
- AT-BRAIN tests pass,
- Professional Session 4 integration passes,
- Codex reports READY FOR M10.

If M9 is incomplete:

```text
STOP → FINISH M9 → REVIEW → COMMIT → BEGIN M10
```

Do not implement evaluation/decision logic on top of unresolved M9 object identity or privacy defects.

---

# 2. M10 Goal

M10 implements structured convergence and explicit human decisions.

The curriculum flow is:

```text
MULTIPLE OPTIONS
↓
DOT VOTING / OTHER DECISION-SUPPORT METHODS
↓
SEE DIFFERENCES
↓
DISCUSS
↓
UNDERSTAND
↓
HUMAN DECISION
↓
DECISION RECORD
```

The core product rule is:

# VOTING DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY FINALIZE A DECISION

A vote is decision-support data.

A Decision Record is a separate human-authored/finalized project record.

---

# 3. M10 Product Boundary

M10 includes:

- `voting_sessions`,
- `voting_options`,
- `votes`,
- Dot Voting MVP,
- configurable vote limit,
- open voting,
- close voting,
- anonymous/hidden/reveal configuration support,
- server-side vote validation,
- voting results,
- `decisions`,
- `decision_options`,
- `decision_participants`,
- `decision_links`,
- create Decision,
- finalize Decision,
- supersede Decision,
- linking Decision to Voting Session,
- linking Decision to Artifacts/Development Objects,
- Evidence link extension point,
- Decision history,
- RLS/security,
- AT-VOTE acceptance tests,
- AT-DEC acceptance tests.

M10 does **not** yet fully implement:

- Fist to Five runtime,
- Planning Poker runtime,
- Evidence subsystem,
- AI,
- Affinity,
- Mind Map,
- Patent tools,
- general Sharing.

The architecture must preserve later support for Fist to Five and Planning Poker.

---

# 4. Curriculum Principle

Professional Course Session 5 teaches that voting is not about winning.

The intended learning pattern is:

```text
Vote
→ See the Differences
→ Discuss
→ Understand
→ Decide
```

Different votes are information.

The platform must not implement:

```text
top vote = automatic final decision
```

unless a future workflow explicitly defines such behavior.

---

# 5. Voting Session Schema

Implement:

```text
voting_sessions
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `activity_instance_id`
- `voting_type`
- `status`
- `vote_limit`
- `anonymous`
- `reveal_mode`
- `created_by`
- `opened_at`
- `closed_at`

Voting types in schema:

```text
DOT_VOTE
FIST_TO_FIVE
PLANNING_POKER
```

MVP M10 requirement:

```text
DOT_VOTE
```

FIST_TO_FIVE and PLANNING_POKER should be schema-compatible but may remain unimplemented at runtime.

---

# 6. Voting Option Schema

Implement:

```text
voting_options
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `voting_session_id`
- `development_object_id` nullable
- `label`
- `description`
- `sequence`

Preferred pattern:

```text
Voting Option
→ existing Development Object
```

Examples:

- Problem,
- Solution,
- Feature,
- Design option,
- Technical direction.

Do not duplicate canonical Problems/Solutions just to vote on them.

---

# 7. Vote Schema

Implement:

```text
votes
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `voting_session_id`
- `voting_option_id`
- `user_id`
- `value`
- `created_at`
- `revealed_at` nullable

For Dot Voting:

- `value` should follow the approved MVP semantics,
- vote limit must be enforced server-side,
- direct database insertion must not bypass limit.

---

# 8. Decision Schema

Implement:

```text
decisions
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `project_id`
- `workspace_id`
- `activity_instance_id` nullable
- `title`
- `question`
- `method`
- `outcome`
- `reasoning`
- `status`
- `decision_owner_user_id`
- `decided_at`

Decision is a persistent Project record.

It is not merely a summary of vote counts.

---

# 9. Decision Options

Implement:

```text
decision_options
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `decision_id`
- `label`
- `description`
- `selected`
- `development_object_id` nullable

A Decision may compare:

- Problems,
- Solutions,
- Features,
- directions,
- other project options.

Selected option must be explicit.

---

# 10. Decision Participants

Implement:

```text
decision_participants
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `decision_id`
- `user_id`
- `role`
- `position` nullable
- `comment` nullable

Purpose:

Preserve who participated and, where captured, their position/comment.

Do not infer platform authority from Decision participant role.

---

# 11. Decision Links

Implement:

```text
decision_links
```

Fields:

- `id`
- `decision_id`
- `linked_entity_type`
- `linked_entity_id`
- `relationship_type`

Decision links may point to:

- Voting Session,
- Artifact,
- Development Object,
- Evidence,
- AI Output.

At M10:

Fully support existing entities:
- Voting Session,
- Artifact,
- Development Object.

Evidence and AI links become fully operational in later milestones.

Do not create fake Evidence/AI records.

---

# 12. Dot Voting MVP

M10 must implement Dot Voting completely.

Minimum workflow:

```text
Create Voting Session
↓
Add Options
↓
Open Voting
↓
Eligible Participants Cast Votes
↓
Enforce Vote Limit
↓
Close Voting
↓
View Result
↓
Discuss
↓
Create / Finalize Human Decision
```

---

# 13. Vote Limit Rule

Acceptance requirement:

If:

```text
vote_limit = 3
```

a user cannot cast a fourth valid vote.

This must be enforced:

- server-side,
- transactionally/concurrency-safe,
- at database/business-operation level.

Frontend counters are not sufficient.

---

# 14. Vote Limit Concurrency

Two near-simultaneous vote requests must not bypass the limit.

Example:

```text
user already has 2 votes
↓
two concurrent vote requests
↓
only one may succeed if limit = 3
```

Required protection may use:

- transaction,
- row/advisory locking,
- serializable logic,
- constrained aggregation strategy,
- other safe repository-standard approach.

Silent over-voting is unacceptable.

---

# 15. Eligible Voter Rule

A user may vote only if authorized for:

```text
Activity Instance
+
Workspace
+
Project
+
Team where applicable
+
Voting Session
```

Do not allow:

```text
same Cohort
=
eligible to vote in every Team
```

Team B cannot vote in Team A.

---

# 16. Open / Closed State

Votes may be cast only while Voting Session is open.

Conceptual lifecycle:

```text
DRAFT / CREATED
↓
OPEN
↓
CLOSED
```

Exact status vocabulary should follow approved repository conventions.

After close:

```text
new votes = denied
```

unless a future authorized reopen policy is explicitly implemented.

---

# 17. Reveal / Anonymous Foundations

Schema supports:

```text
anonymous
reveal_mode
revealed_at
```

The API includes:

```text
revealVotingSession()
```

especially for Planning Poker or hidden voting modes.

M10 Dot Voting must respect configured visibility.

Do not expose hidden individual vote details before reveal when configuration forbids it.

Do not confuse:

```text
anonymous to participants
```

with:

```text
no auditability in database
```

The system may still need user identity internally for limit enforcement and integrity.

---

# 18. Voting Results

Voting results may include:

- count,
- distribution,
- option order,
- participant summary where policy allows.

But results must not automatically mutate:

- selected Solution,
- accepted Idea,
- Project baseline,
- Decision outcome.

Human finalization remains separate.

---

# 19. Decision Creation Contract

Approved:

```text
createDecision(input)
```

Input:

```text
projectId
workspaceId
activityInstanceId optional
title
question
method
options
```

The Decision should initially be non-final until `finalizeDecision()`.

---

# 20. Decision Finalization Contract

Approved:

```text
finalizeDecision(input)
```

Input:

```text
decisionId
selectedOptionId optional
outcome
reasoning
linkedEvidenceIds optional
linkedArtifactIds optional
linkedObjectIds optional
```

Critical rule:

```text
Voting result alone must not automatically finalize a decision.
Human finalization required.
```

---

# 21. Decision Reasoning Requirement

AT-DEC-001 requires finalized Decision to store:

- issue/question,
- outcome,
- reasoning,
- participants,
- linked evidence,
- timestamp.

Evidence subsystem is M12.

Therefore M10 should:

- support Decision Links structurally,
- fully link existing Artifacts/Objects/Voting,
- preserve Evidence extension point,
- complete Evidence-specific acceptance after M12 if no Evidence table exists yet.

Do not invent Evidence rows.

---

# 22. Supersede Decision

Approved:

```text
supersedeDecision(input)
```

Rule:

A later Decision may supersede an earlier Decision.

Earlier Decision remains in history.

Never:

```text
DELETE old decision
```

or:

```text
overwrite old outcome
```

Use an explicit relationship/history mechanism.

---

# 23. Decision History Principle

Project decision history must answer:

```text
What was decided?
Why?
By whom?
When?
Based on what?
What replaced it later?
```

This supports long-term invention traceability.

---

# 24. Session 5 Output

The Professional Course Session 5 curriculum says to save:

- Selected Problem(s),
- Selected Solution(s),
- Selected Feature(s),
- Decision Reasoning.

The platform should represent this with:

```text
Decision Record
+
Decision Options
+
Development Object links
+
Voting Session link
```

and optionally a `TEAM_DECISION_RECORD` Artifact using M8.

Do not store only a screenshot of vote results.

---

# 25. Team Decision Record Artifact

Where the approved Activity Definition expects an Artifact output:

```text
TEAM_DECISION_RECORD
```

M10 should compose it using:

- Decision Record,
- linked selected Project Objects,
- reasoning,
- linked Voting Session,
- Artifact/Version system from M8.

Decision remains canonical structured data.

Artifact is the versioned higher-level output.

---

# 26. Source-of-Truth Files

Before each M10 task, Codex must read:

```text
/docs/03_ROLES_PERMISSIONS.md
/docs/04_WORKSPACE_TEAM_COLLABORATION.md
/docs/05_DEVELOPMENT_PROJECT_MODEL.md

/docs/21_CODEX_M7_PROMPTS.md
/docs/22_CODEX_M8_PROMPTS.md
/docs/23_CODEX_M9_PROMPTS.md
```

Also read the approved Professional Course Session 5 material.

---

# 27. Global Codex Header

Use this block at the beginning of every M10 task if project rules are not automatically retained:

```text
You are implementing the FICI Invention Education & Development Platform.

Before making changes:

1. Read the relevant /docs files and approved Session 5 curriculum.
2. Treat them as source of truth.
3. Do not invent missing business rules.
4. M10 MVP fully implements DOT_VOTE.
5. Preserve schema compatibility for FIST_TO_FIVE and PLANNING_POKER without pretending they are implemented.
6. Voting is decision support, not automatic final decision.
7. Human finalization is required for Decision Records.
8. Enforce vote limits server-side and concurrency-safely.
9. Preserve Team/Workspace/Project isolation.
10. Never trust client-provided voter identity, participant role, Decision owner, or vote count.
11. Reuse canonical Development Objects as options.
12. Do not duplicate Problems/Solutions for voting.
13. Preserve Decision history and supersession.
14. Use existing Activity Engine and Artifact/Version system.
15. Do not build M11+ Affinity/Mind Map or M12 Evidence.
16. Use migrations for schema changes.
17. Use strict TypeScript.
18. Validate runtime input.
19. If requirements conflict or are ambiguous, STOP → FLAG → ASK.
20. Run required validation before finishing.
21. Report:
    - files changed,
    - migrations,
    - operations,
    - vote-limit enforcement,
    - concurrency handling,
    - Decision finalization rules,
    - RLS,
    - tests,
    - results,
    - assumptions,
    - deferred later voting types,
    - unresolved issues.
```

# 46. M10.19 — Voting/Decision Concurrency Tests

## Objective

Prevent race conditions affecting voting integrity or Decision finalization.

## Copy/Paste Prompt

```text
TASK ID: M10.19
TASK: Voting & Decision Concurrency

OBJECTIVE

Test concurrency-sensitive cases.

CASE 1 — VOTE LIMIT

User has 2/3 votes.
Two simultaneous vote requests.
Expected:
- one succeeds,
- one fails,
- total <= 3.

CASE 2 — CLOSE VS VOTE

Vote request races with Session close.
Expected:
- deterministic transaction outcome,
- no vote accepted after committed close.

CASE 3 — DOUBLE FINALIZE

Two finalizeDecision() requests.
Expected:
- one canonical finalization,
- no contradictory outcomes.

CASE 4 — SUPERSEDE RACE

Two newer Decisions attempt to supersede same current Decision if system has a current-decision concept.
Expected:
- no silent contradictory history.

Use transaction/state preconditions/locking consistent with repository architecture.

DEFINITION OF DONE

No last-write-wins corruption in voting or Decision finalization.
```

```text
- AT-DEC-001 PASS for M10-owned fields
- AT-DEC-002 PASS
- Session 5 integration PASS
- zero vote-limit bypass
- zero cross-Team leak
- zero automatic Decision finalization
- no M11+ scope creep

FINAL REPORT

Return:
1. security review
2. integrity review
3. issues found
4. issues fixed
5. remaining issues
6. BLOCKER status
7. tests/results
8. recommendation: READY FOR M11 or NOT READY FOR M11
```

---

# 49. Voting Type vs Decision Method

Do not conflate:

```text
voting_type
```

with:

```text
decision.method
```

Voting type describes the structured voting mechanic.

Decision method describes how the Team actually finalized its Decision.

Example:

```text
Voting Type = DOT_VOTE
Decision Method = discussion_after_dot_vote
```

if such method value is approved.

---

# 50. Dot Voting Semantics

Dot Voting is for prioritization.

It is not proof of:

- correctness,
- technical feasibility,
- patentability,
- safety,
- business viability.

Do not label highest votes as "best solution" automatically.

---

# 51. Fist to Five

Schema supports:

```text
FIST_TO_FIVE
```

Curriculum uses it to measure support and reveal concerns.

M10 architecture should allow it later.

Do not implement incomplete Fist-to-Five behavior and mark it production-ready unless explicitly required.

---

# 52. Planning Poker

Schema supports:

```text
PLANNING_POKER
```

Curriculum uses it for team estimation, not popularity voting.

Future implementation must preserve:

```text
estimate independently
→ reveal together
→ discuss differences
→ estimate again
```

M10 should preserve reveal architecture but need not implement full Planning Poker runtime.

---

# 53. Vote Value

`votes.value` exists because different voting methods need different values.

For Dot Voting, if the approved business rule is one dot per cast:

```text
value = 1
```

or equivalent.

Do not invent weighted Dot Voting unless source docs approve it.

---

# 54. Duplicate Vote on Same Option

The schema does not by itself state whether one user may place multiple dots on one option.

Do not silently choose.

If Session 5 or Activity config does not resolve it:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

Possible future configurations may include:

- one vote per option,
- multiple dots allowed per option.

This affects uniqueness constraints.

---

# 55. Anonymous Voting

Anonymous participant display does not mean anonymous database identity.

The system still needs user identity for:

- eligibility,
- vote-limit enforcement,
- abuse prevention,
- audit where authorized.

Participant-facing queries may hide identity.

---

# 56. Reveal Mode

Exact `reveal_mode` vocabulary is not fully defined in the schema.

Do not invent permanent values without source support.

A safe typed model may be introduced only if consistent with Activity configuration and documented.

If unclear:

```text
FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 57. Reopen Voting

API says close locks votes unless reopened by authorized role, but a dedicated reopen contract is not specified.

Do not invent reopen behavior unless required.

M10 may safely omit reopen and treat close as final for MVP.

---

# 58. Decision Owner

`decision_owner_user_id` is the accountable owner/finalizer context.

Do not allow client spoofing.

Ownership does not necessarily mean sole participant.

---

# 59. Decision Participants

Decision Participants preserve involvement.

They do not automatically grant:

- Project access,
- Workspace access,
- approval authority.

Canonical permissions remain authoritative.

---

# 60. Decision Selected Option

Voting winner and Decision selected option are separate.

Example:

```text
Option A = highest votes
Human Decision selects Option B
Reasoning = technical risk discovered during discussion
```

The data model must support this.

---

# 61. Decision Links to Evidence — Deferred Integration

M10 supports the link shape.

M12 implements Evidence Records.

Do not mark full linked-evidence behavior complete until Evidence exists.

When M12 arrives, it should extend AT-DEC-001's Evidence link sub-check.

---

# 62. Decision Links to Artifacts

M10 can fully link:

- Problem Bank,
- Solution Bank,
- Team Decision Record,
- other authorized M8 Artifacts.

This helps show which structured outputs informed the Decision.

---

# 63. Decision Links to Voting

A Decision should be able to say:

```text
informed by Voting Session V123
```

This retains method traceability.

Do not copy all votes into Decision JSON unnecessarily.

---

# 64. Supersession

A later Decision can replace an earlier one.

Preferred history:

```text
D1 — finalized
D2 — finalized
D2 SUPERSEDES D1
```

D1 remains queryable.

---

# 65. Decision vs Artifact Approval

A Team Decision is not the same as Master Artifact Approval.

Example:

```text
Team decides Solution S3
```

then:

```text
Team Decision Record Artifact submitted
Master approves Artifact
```

These are separate events with separate authority.

---

# 66. Decision vs Project Baseline

Finalizing a Decision does not automatically update Project baseline unless a later explicit workflow says so.

Do not silently change baseline from a Decision.

---

# 67. Voting and Activity Engine

Voting Session must belong to an Activity Instance.

Use M7 for:

- participants,
- Project/Workspace/Team context,
- status/dependencies.

Do not build a standalone voting product detached from Activity scope.

---

# 68. Decision and Activity Output

A finalized Decision may become:

- Activity Output via Decision link/ID,
- Team Decision Record Artifact,
- input to later Activities.

Use the existing Activity Output extension point when Decision entity support is available.

---

# 69. Audit / Change Log

Recommended M10 events include:

```text
VOTING_SESSION_CREATED
VOTING_OPENED
VOTING_CLOSED
DECISION_CREATED
DECISION_FINALIZED
DECISION_SUPERSEDED
```

Do not log individual hidden vote values into broad audit metadata if that would violate anonymous/reveal policy.

Project Change Log may record meaningful finalized Decision changes.

---

# 70. M10 Expected Repository Additions

Conceptually:

```text
features/
├── voting/
│   ├── sessions/
│   ├── options/
│   ├── votes/
│   ├── results/
│   ├── access/
│   └── validation/
└── decisions/
    ├── operations/
    ├── options/
    ├── participants/
    ├── links/
    ├── supersession/
    └── access/

lib/
├── permissions/
│   ├── voting.ts
│   └── decision.ts
├── concurrency/
│   └── vote-limit.ts
└── traceability/

supabase/
├── migrations/
│   ├── ...voting_sessions...
│   ├── ...voting_options...
│   ├── ...votes...
│   ├── ...decisions...
│   ├── ...decision_options...
│   ├── ...decision_participants...
│   ├── ...decision_links...
│   └── ...m10_rls...
└── tests/
    └── rls/
        ├── voting...
        └── decisions...

tests/
├── unit/
│   ├── voting/
│   └── decisions/
├── integration/
│   ├── voting/
│   ├── decisions/
│   └── session5/
└── e2e/
    └── professional-session5.spec.ts
```

Exact paths may vary.

---

# 71. M10 Completion Gate

M10 is complete only when:

```text
[ ] voting_sessions exists
[ ] voting_options exists
[ ] votes exists

[ ] DOT_VOTE fully implemented
[ ] createVotingSession() implemented
[ ] openVotingSession() implemented
[ ] castVote() implemented
[ ] closeVotingSession() implemented
[ ] reveal foundation implemented where configured
[ ] result query implemented

[ ] vote limit enforced server-side
[ ] concurrent requests cannot exceed limit
[ ] unauthorized Team cannot vote
[ ] hidden vote rules enforced
[ ] closed Session rejects votes

[ ] voting does not auto-finalize Decision

[ ] decisions exists
[ ] decision_options exists
[ ] decision_participants exists
[ ] decision_links exists

[ ] createDecision() implemented
[ ] finalizeDecision() implemented
[ ] supersedeDecision() implemented

[ ] outcome/reasoning persisted
[ ] participants persisted
[ ] voting link supported
[ ] Artifact/Object links supported
[ ] Evidence link extension point preserved

[ ] Team Decision Record Artifact integration works where configured

[ ] Decision history survives supersession
[ ] direct client cannot forge final Decision
[ ] Team B cannot access Team A Decision
[ ] removed member denied future Team scope

[ ] AT-VOTE-001 PASS
[ ] AT-VOTE-002 PASS
[ ] AT-VOTE-003 PASS

[ ] AT-DEC-001 PASS for M10-owned fields
[ ] AT-DEC-002 PASS

[ ] Professional Session 5 integration PASS

[ ] lint passes
[ ] typecheck passes
[ ] unit tests pass
[ ] integration tests pass
[ ] E2E tests pass
[ ] RLS tests pass
[ ] concurrency tests pass
[ ] build passes

[ ] no M11+ feature implemented prematurely
[ ] Codex reports READY FOR M11
```

Any vote-limit bypass is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

Any cross-Team voting access is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

Any automatic vote→Decision finalization is:

```text
ARCHITECTURE DEFECT
```

---

# 72. Recommended Commit Sequence

Example:

```text
feat(voting): add Voting schema
feat(voting): add create/open operations
feat(voting): add secure Dot Vote casting
feat(voting): add reveal/result/close behavior
feat(decisions): add Decision schema
feat(decisions): add Decision creation
feat(decisions): add human finalization
feat(decisions): add Decision links
feat(decisions): add supersession history
feat(artifacts): add Team Decision Record integration
feat(security): add Voting/Decision RLS
test(voting): add AT-VOTE suite
test(decisions): add AT-DEC suite
test(session5): add Professional Session 5 flow
test(concurrency): add vote-limit races
test(security): add cross-Team Voting/Decision leakage tests
chore(security): complete M10 hardening
```

---

# 73. M10 Non-Goals

Do not accept these as "helpful additions" during M10:

- full Fist to Five runtime,
- full Planning Poker runtime,
- Affinity groups,
- Mind Map,
- React Flow,
- Liveblocks,
- Evidence records,
- Patent Workspace,
- AI Assistant,
- Sharing,
- automatic winner selection,
- automatic Project baseline update from voting,
- automatic Decision finalization,
- autonomous team decision-making.

---

# 74. Potential M10 Ambiguities Codex Must Flag

Do not silently decide if approved docs do not resolve:

- exact Voting Session status vocabulary,
- exact reveal_mode values,
- whether Dot Voting is live-result or hidden by default,
- whether Dot Voting is anonymous by default,
- whether a user may place multiple dots on one option,
- whether vote_limit counts total dots or number of distinct options,
- whether votes may be changed/retracted while open,
- whether closed Voting may be reopened,
- who may create Voting Session besides Master,
- whether Team Lead may open/close/reveal,
- whether Master may vote,
- whether Mentor may vote,
- whether Activity host is a distinct participant role,
- exact Decision status vocabulary,
- exact Decision method vocabulary,
- who may finalize Team Decision,
- whether Team Lead alone may finalize,
- whether final Decision requires all participants,
- whether Decision requires a selectedOptionId,
- whether multiple options may be selected,
- whether participant positions are mandatory,
- whether superseded Decision remains "finalized" plus superseded or changes status,
- whether final Decision automatically creates TEAM_DECISION_RECORD Artifact,
- whether Team Decision Record requires Master approval,
- whether Decision Evidence links wait until M12,
- whether Decision changes Project baseline automatically.

If unresolved:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 75. Recommended Safe Defaults for Purely Technical Decisions

Only where they do not alter approved product policy:

- UUID IDs,
- server-derived voter identity,
- server-derived Decision owner identity,
- DOT_VOTE runtime only,
- future voting types preserved in enum/schema,
- vote limit checked transactionally,
- closed Session rejects new votes,
- no auto-finalization,
- canonical Project Objects referenced rather than copied,
- Decision history preserved,
- supersession uses explicit relationship/history,
- Team/Workspace/Project RLS enforced,
- direct DB identity spoof blocked,
- no Evidence records until M12.

---

# 76. Review Checklist for Ahmad/FICI

Before implementation, confirm M10 reflects the intended Session 5 model:

```text
1. M10 fully implements Dot Voting.

2. Fist to Five and Planning Poker remain future-compatible.

15. Session 5 can produce a Team Decision Record Artifact.

16. M10 does not yet build Affinity, Mind Map, Evidence, Patent, AI, or Sharing.
```


For M10:
