---

# 53. Daily vs FICI Session

Do not conflate:

```text
Daily Room
```

with:

```text
FICI Course Session / Activity
```

Daily Room is media infrastructure.

FICI Session/Activity is educational workflow.

---

# 54. Join Token vs FICI Session

A join token is temporary media access.

It is not:

- enrollment,
- Team membership,
- Activity participation record,
- course completion,
- Workspace permission.

---

# 55. Provider Room ID vs Permission

Knowing:

```text
room name
room URL
provider room ID
```

must not be enough to join a private class.

FICI authorization + provider join capability is required.

---

# 56. Room Creation vs Activity Launch

Creating live room does not necessarily launch Activity.

Master uses normal M7 operation for Activity lifecycle.

---

# 57. Video Presence vs Attendance

Being connected to video does not automatically mean:

- present for entire class,
- completed Session,
- completed Activity.

Do not infer educational completion from media connection.

---

# 58. Breakout vs Team Membership

Provider breakout assignment must follow current FICI Team membership.

Do not maintain an independent permanent breakout-member list in Daily.

---

# 59. Live Session vs Team Chat

FICI Team Chat remains persistent communication.

Daily media/chat is ephemeral/provider-controlled unless later product policy explicitly captures it.

---

# 60. Recording

Recording is out of scope.

Do not enable automatic recording.

Do not create recording storage/retention assumptions.

---

# 61. Screen Sharing

Daily may provide screen sharing as a media feature.

Using screen share must not grant access to FICI private resources.

It is the presenter's visual media action only.

---

# 62. Master Moderation

Do not assume full Zoom-like moderation is required.

Implement only provider controls required for secure pilot operation.

Advanced moderation is later scope.

---

# 63. Guest Access

Public/anonymous guest access is not part of M16.

All pilot users must authenticate through FICI unless later policy explicitly adds guests.

---

# 64. External Invite Links

Do not email/share raw unrestricted Daily room URLs as authentication.

Notifications may link to FICI live-classroom route.

The route authenticates/authorizes and then issues join capability.

---

# 65. Notifications Integration

M15 may optionally notify Cohort users that live class is available only if an approved event exists.

M16 does not require building new reminder scheduling.

Do not create calendar/reminder system.

---

# 66. Provider Webhooks

Daily webhooks are optional in M16.

If used:

- verify signatures,
- handle idempotently,
- store only needed provider events,
- do not let provider event directly mutate canonical Activity completion.

Do not add webhooks without a concrete M16 need.

---

# 67. Room End State

Exact meaning of "end live room" is not defined.

Do not silently decide:

- whether Master destroys room,
- expires room,
- reuses room next class,
- simply leaves.

If explicit end-room behavior is required:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 68. Room Scheduling

M16 does not require a calendar scheduler.

Room may be created on demand for current Course Session.

Do not build Calendar integration.

---

# 69. Live Session Notifications

M16 does not require push/email reminders.

If the pilot later requires "class starts in 10 minutes", this is separate scheduling/notification functionality.

Do not invent it.

---

# 70. Provider Usage / Cost

M16 does not require detailed cost analytics.

If Daily returns usage metadata, it may be logged technically.

Do not build billing dashboard.

---

# 71. Browser Permissions

Live classroom UI must handle:

- camera permission denied,
- microphone permission denied,
- device unavailable,
- browser unsupported/limited.

Provide clear user-facing states.

Do not treat device-denial as FICI authorization failure.

---

# 72. Browser Acceptance

M17 performs broad browser release testing.

M16 should at least test the supported pilot browsers where feasible for embedded Daily experience.

Do not claim universal browser support without testing.

---

# 73. Mobile / Responsive

Complex structured work is primarily desktop/tablet.

M16 live room should remain usable on reasonable mobile view, but do not redesign the full platform for mobile during M16.

---

# 74. Accessibility

M16 surrounding FICI controls must support:

- keyboard access,
- meaningful labels,
- visible focus,
- clear join/leave/error controls.

Provider accessibility depends on Daily component capabilities.

Document provider limitations rather than hiding them.

---

# 75. Privacy / Consent

Video/audio introduces privacy considerations.

M16 product docs do not define recording/consent policy.

Therefore:

- no automatic recording,
- no hidden recording,
- no attendance surveillance,
- no background transcript capture.

Flag any requested recording feature for policy review.

---

# 76. M16 Expected Repository Additions

Conceptually:

```text
features/
└── live-classroom/
    ├── provider/
    ├── rooms/
    ├── tokens/
    ├── authorization/
    ├── breakout/
    ├── activity-link/
    └── ui/

lib/
├── live-classroom/
│   ├── provider.ts
│   ├── daily-provider.ts
│   ├── room-mapping.ts
│   └── join-authorization.ts
└── permissions/
    └── live-classroom.ts

tests/
├── unit/
│   └── live-classroom/
├── integration/
│   ├── live-room/
│   └── breakout/
└── e2e/
    └── live-classroom.spec.ts
```

Database migration is required only if a dedicated FICI live-room mapping table is approved/necessary.

Do not add schema solely for convenience.

---

# 77. M16 Completion Gate

M16 is complete only when:

```text
[ ] Daily integration exists
[ ] Daily is behind provider abstraction
[ ] DAILY_API_KEY is server-only

[ ] Master can get/create Cohort live room
[ ] unrelated Master denied
[ ] Student cannot create room

[ ] authorized Student can obtain join token
[ ] unauthorized Cohort user denied
[ ] client cannot spoof Master role
[ ] room ID alone does not grant access
[ ] token is temporary/minimal

[ ] live classroom UI works
[ ] current Activity is linked
[ ] FICI Activity remains canonical
[ ] joining/leaving does not auto-complete Activity
[ ] Project/Artifact state remains in FICI

[ ] optional breakout mapping works OR explicitly deferred
[ ] Team breakout authorization works if enabled
[ ] removed member cannot obtain new breakout token
[ ] Master breakout navigation works if enabled

[ ] Daily chat does not replace Team Chat
[ ] no advanced recording management
[ ] no custom WebRTC stack

[ ] provider failure does not corrupt FICI state
[ ] room creation is retry/idempotency safe
[ ] provider secret exposure test passes
[ ] Live Classroom E2E passes

[ ] lint passes
[ ] typecheck passes
[ ] unit tests pass
[ ] integration tests pass
[ ] E2E tests pass
[ ] build passes

[ ] no M17 scope implemented prematurely
[ ] Codex reports READY FOR M17
```

Any unauthorized room/token access is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

Any provider secret exposed to client is:

```text
BLOCKER
```

Any video-provider event mutating canonical educational state incorrectly is:

```text
ARCHITECTURE DEFECT
```

---

# 78. Recommended Commit Sequence

Example:

```text
feat(live): add live-classroom provider abstraction
feat(live): add Daily provider adapter
feat(live): add room mapping strategy
feat(live): add Master get/create room
feat(live): add Student join authorization
feat(live): add temporary join tokens
feat(live): add embedded classroom UI
feat(live): link current Activity
feat(live): add optional Team breakout mapping
feat(live): add breakout authorization
feat(live): add Master breakout navigation
test(live): add Cohort room security tests
test(live): add member-removal token tests
test(live): add provider failure/idempotency tests
test(security): add Daily secret exposure tests
test(e2e): add live-classroom pilot flow
chore(security): complete M16 hardening
```

---

# 79. M16 Non-Goals

Do not accept these as "helpful additions" during M16:

- custom WebRTC stack,
- custom SFU/media servers,
- Zoom parity,
- video recording library,
- transcription,
- AI meeting assistant,
- automatic notes,
- attendance scoring,
- student behavior analytics,
- public guest rooms,
- webinar mode,
- calendar scheduling,
- email reminders,
- custom media routing,
- M17 full release hardening.

---

# 80. Potential M16 Ambiguities Codex Must Flag

Do not silently decide if approved docs do not resolve:

- whether one Daily room is reused across Course Sessions,
- whether each class occurrence gets a new room,
- exact FICI schema for provider room mapping,
- whether Master can explicitly end/destroy a room,
- join-token lifetime,
- Master Daily permission claims,
- Student Daily permission claims,
- screen-share rights,
- whether Daily chat is enabled,
- whether recording is enabled,
- whether attendance is tracked,
- whether join/leave events are stored,
- whether Team breakout rooms are required for pilot,
- whether breakouts are created automatically or on demand,
- whether Mentor may join Team breakouts,
- whether Admin may join live Cohort room,
- whether users outside Cohort can be invited as guests,
- whether live room availability sends notification,
- whether Course Session has scheduled start/end time,
- whether provider webhooks are required,
- how to reconcile provider-created room if local mapping write fails.

If unresolved:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

---

# 81. Recommended Safe Defaults for Purely Technical Decisions

Only where they do not alter approved product policy:

- Daily behind provider abstraction,
- server-only API key,
- Daily Prebuilt for MVP,
- private/token-gated rooms,
- server-derived participant identity,
- temporary join tokens,
- provider room IDs treated as integration metadata,
- no automatic recording,
- no guest access,
- no attendance inference,
- no Activity mutation on join/leave,
- explicit FICI authorization before every token issuance,
- Team breakout access from current Team membership,
- provider failure isolated from FICI state,
- no M17 scope.

Prepare the platform for a real Professional Course pilot.

# 3. M17 Release Rule

The release rule is exact:

# NO OPEN BLOCKER DEFECT

A pilot must not launch with a known BLOCKER.

This includes, among others:

- cross-Team private data leak,
- Personal Workspace leak,
- unauthorized approval,
- AI unauthorized-context leak,
- private File access bypass,
- approved Artifact mutation,
- direct-ID bypass,
- contradictory final transaction state,
- unshared resource exposure.

HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW issues may remain only if:

- documented,
- impact understood,
- workaround known where necessary,
- Ahmad/FICI explicitly accepts the risk for pilot.

---

# 58. Full E2E Must Use Real Role Boundaries

Do not execute the entire E2E as one privileged service role.

Use actual test identities:

```text
Admin
Master
Mentor where relevant
Student A1
Student A2
Student B1
Student B2
```

Switch identities as the real product would.

Otherwise permission behavior is not tested.

---

# 59. Release Test Fixtures

Use the standard acceptance fixture where defined:

```text
Professional Course — Test Cohort

Team A
Team B

Project A → Team A
Project B → Team B

Personal Workspace per Student
```

Use stable fixtures to make security tests reproducible.

---

# 60. Never Weaken RLS to Fix E2E

If a feature works only after broadening an RLS policy such as:

```text
authenticated users can SELECT all
```

the fix is invalid.

Instead:

```text
identify required scope
→ authorize exactly
→ test positive and negative paths
```

---

# 61. Never Replace Server Authorization With UI Hiding

Example invalid fix:

```text
Hide "Approve" button from Students
```

if Students can still call approval endpoint.

M17 must attack backend directly.

---

# 62. Never Replace Database Security With API Security Alone

For protected data, application authorization and RLS should reinforce each other where the architecture requires RLS.

A direct authenticated database query must still be safe.

---

# 63. Never Fix Privacy Leak by Obscuring IDs

UUIDs reduce guessing.

They do not provide authorization.

Known valid IDs must still fail for unauthorized users.

---

# 64. Error Response Safety

For protected resources, safe outcomes include:

```text
FORBIDDEN
```

or:

```text
NOT_FOUND
```

depending on established API semantics.

Do not return:

```text
"Artifact exists but belongs to Team A"
```

to Team B.

---

# 65. Historical Attribution

M17 must protect the principle:

```text
Access can end.
History remains.
```

Removed user contributions stay attributed.

Do not anonymize/delete authorship as an authorization fix unless policy requires it.

---

# 66. Approval Integrity

Approval is a high-risk multi-step operation.

The final state must never contain contradictions such as:

```text
Version = APPROVED
but
Artifact.current_version_id = old version
```

or:

```text
notification says approved
but transaction rolled back
```

AT-TX-001 must actively inject failure.

---

# 67. Share Revocation Integrity

After Share revocation:

- future entity access denied,
- future signed File access denied,
- future AI context denied,
- Share history retained,
- notification history may remain,
- recipient does not gain source Workspace.

Retest all integrations, not only M13 endpoint.

---

# 68. AI Provider Payload Is the Security Boundary

A response filter is too late.

Unauthorized content must not be sent to provider in the first place.

M17 must inspect provider payloads in tests.

---

# 69. File URLs Are Capabilities

Signed File URLs should:

- be temporary,
- be issued after authorization,
- not be stored as permanent public references.

Do not log reusable signed URLs broadly.

---

# 70. Realtime Is Not Canonical

For:

- chat,
- notifications,
- Affinity,
- Mind Map,

disconnect/reconnect must recover from canonical saved state.

Realtime event loss must not equal data loss.

---

# 71. Liveblocks Is Not Canonical

Mind Map/Affinity final saved state must remain reconstructable from PostgreSQL/Artifact Versions.

If Liveblocks is unavailable, previously saved canonical work must remain.

---

# 72. Daily Is Not Canonical

Live video outage must not affect:

- Projects,
- Activities,
- Artifacts,
- Decisions,
- course state.

---

# 73. OpenAI Is Not Canonical

AI provider outage must not affect existing Project history.

Saved AI Outputs belong to FICI database.

---

# 74. Resend Is Not Canonical

Email delivery failure must not roll back:

- Submission,
- Review,
- Approval,
- Team membership,
- Share.

In-app canonical state remains.

---

# 75. Backup Test Must Be Real

A backup checkbox cannot be satisfied by:

```text
"Supabase says backups exist"
```

At least one non-production restore test is required.

---

# 76. File Recovery Limitation Must Be Explicit

Database backup and object-storage recovery are not necessarily the same.

Document:

- database restore,
- storage restore/export,
- irreversible limitations,
- manual steps.

Do not imply storage recovery exists if untested.

---

# 77. Logging Must Not Become a Data Leak

Structured logs can leak data.

Redact/minimize:

- secrets,
- tokens,
- signed URLs,
- private prompts,
- private files,
- full chat content,
- raw Evidence.

---

# 78. Rate Limiting Is Defense-in-Depth

Rate limiting does not replace:

- auth,
- authorization,
- validation,
- RLS.

A slow unauthorized attack is still unauthorized.

---

# 79. File Size and MIME Limits

Exact product-facing limits may be configuration values.

M17 should verify:

- a limit exists,
- it is enforced server-side,
- oversized files fail safely.

If exact values remain open, record them as configuration requiring Ahmad/FICI approval.

Do not invent business limits silently.

---

# 80. Accessibility Is a Release Quality Requirement

Do not treat accessibility only as post-pilot polish.

Fix straightforward HIGH-impact issues such as:

- unlabeled form fields,
- inaccessible dialog focus,
- no keyboard submission,
- status shown only by color.

Complex canvas alternative may remain a documented limitation if the structured alternative is practical.

---

# 81. Browser Testing Must Include Real Provider Components

Where feasible, include:

- Liveblocks collaborative tool,
- Daily embedded room,
- AI UI,
- signed file flows.

A page-only smoke test is insufficient.

---

# 82. Performance Is Practical, Not Enterprise SLA

M17 should measure realistic pilot behavior.

Do not redesign architecture for millions of users.

Only fix performance problems that materially impair pilot use.

---

# 83. Release Candidate Versioning

The final report must name:

- Git commit SHA,
- deployment URL/environment,
- migration state,
- release date/time,
- test-run identifier.

Do not release from an untracked local tree.

---

# 84. Clean Working Tree

Before final release:

```text
git status
```

should show no accidental uncommitted release code.

Generated local debug files/secrets must not be committed.

---

# 85. Secret Scan

Search for accidental secrets:

- Supabase service role key
- OpenAI key
- Daily API key
- Resend key
- Liveblocks secret
- tokens/passwords

Check:

- repository files
- tests
- snapshots
- logs
- example env
- client bundle references

Any real secret committed:
BLOCKER until revoked/rotated and removed appropriately.

---

# 86. Production Data Safety

M17 tests should primarily run in isolated test/staging environments.

Do not:

- destructively run rollback tests on production,
- restore over production,
- create fake pilot artifacts in production unless explicitly planned,
- expose real user confidential data in screenshots/logs.

---

# 87. Security Defect Fix Rule

When a BLOCKER is found:

```text
REPRODUCE
→ IDENTIFY ROOT CAUSE
→ FIX
→ ADD REGRESSION TEST
→ RERUN RELATED SUITE
→ RERUN RELEASE-GATE SCENARIO
```

Do not merely patch the exact test input.

---

# 88. Documentation Contradiction Rule

If code behavior required to pass one acceptance test contradicts another approved document:

```text
STOP
→ DOCUMENT CONFLICT
→ IDENTIFY BOTH SOURCES
→ ASK AHMAD/FICI FOR DECISION
```

Do not invent precedence.

---

# 89. Remaining HIGH Issues

A HIGH issue may be pilot-acceptable only if explicitly reviewed.

Final report must state:

- why it remains,
- user impact,
- workaround,
- risk,
- owner,
- post-pilot plan.

Do not bury HIGH issues inside notes.

---

# 90. Remaining MEDIUM / LOW Issues

These may be accepted for pilot but must remain visible in backlog/report.

Examples:

- polish,
- minor browser inconsistency,
- non-critical wording,
- low-impact layout issue.

---

# 91. Pilot Operational Runbook

M17 should leave a lightweight runbook covering:

```text
Deploy
Rollback
Check logs
Check Supabase
Check provider status
Restore database
Disable/limit AI if provider issue
Handle failed email
Handle Daily outage
Support user login/reset
Resolve Team membership mistake
```

Do not create a huge enterprise operations manual.

---

# 92. Provider Outage Behavior

Document expected fallback:

## Supabase issue
Core platform may be unavailable.

## OpenAI issue
AI unavailable; existing project work remains.

## Liveblocks issue
High-frequency collaboration unavailable; saved data remains.

## Daily issue
Video unavailable; structured FICI work remains.

## Resend issue
Email unavailable; in-app state remains.

## Vercel issue
Web app unavailable.

This helps pilot support distinguish critical vs partial outages.

---

# 93. Incident Classification

For pilot support, classify incidents simply:

```text
SECURITY/PRIVACY
DATA INTEGRITY
AUTH/ACCESS
CORE WORKFLOW
PROVIDER OUTAGE
PERFORMANCE
USABILITY
```

Security/privacy incidents receive immediate release/operation priority.

---

# 94. Post-Pilot Success Indicators

After launch, evaluate the source-defined product validation indicators:

- users understand Workspace scope,
- students move selected work Personal → Team,
- instructors review without outside tools,
- structured outputs are reused,
- teams use private chat,
- AI suggestions are understandable and distinguished,
- privacy incidents = zero,
- version history is useful,
- platform reduces disconnected tools/files,
- participants complete Professional Course workflow.

These are post-pilot product signals, not M17 release tests.

---

# 95. M17 Expected Repository Additions

Conceptually:

```text
docs/
├── PILOT_READINESS_REPORT.md
├── RELEASE_RUNBOOK.md
├── BACKUP_RESTORE_RUNBOOK.md
└── KNOWN_ISSUES.md

tests/

│   ├── file-access/

    ├── professional-course-core.spec.ts
    ├── privacy.spec.ts
    ├── member-removal.spec.ts
    └── ai-governance.spec.ts
```

Exact paths may vary.

M17 should mostly add:
- tests,
- fixes,
- docs,
- configuration hardening.

Not new product domains.

---

# 96. Recommended Commit Sequence

Example:

```text
test(release): add acceptance inventory
test(security): expand RLS release suite
test(security): add direct-id matrix
test(security): add E2E privacy attacks
test(security): add member-removal release test
test(ai): rerun leakage/provider-payload suite
test(transaction): add approval rollback matrix
test(concurrency): add competing-state release tests
fix(security): resolve discovered authorization defects
fix(integrity): resolve transaction/history defects
fix(files): harden limits/access
feat(security): add required rate limits
fix(errors): harden safe error handling
chore(logging): add structured safe logging
test(accessibility): add release checklist
test(browser): add supported browser matrix
docs(ops): add backup/restore runbook
test(recovery): record non-production restore result
test(e2e): add full Professional Course release scenario
docs(release): add pilot readiness report
```

Commit names may differ.

---

# 97. M17 Non-Goals

Do not add:

- new Advanced Course modules,
- investor CRM,
- marketplace,
- new patent engine,
- public sharing,
- public profiles,
- social feed,
- complex analytics,
- new AI agent framework,
- AI voting,
- automatic grading,
- recording/transcription system,
- calendar platform,
- mobile-native app,
- enterprise SSO,
- billing/subscription,
- multi-tenant institution administration beyond existing approved model.

---

# 98. Potential M17 Ambiguities Codex Must Flag

Do not silently decide:

- exact file size limits if still unresolved,
- exact AI usage quotas,
- exact email event policy if unresolved,
- data retention periods,
- notification retention,
- recording/attendance policy,
- final CSP domains if provider configuration differs,
- whether Sentry is required for pilot,
- exact HIGH-issue acceptance authority,
- restore RTO/RPO targets,
- supported browser version cutoff,
- exact mobile support commitment.

If required for release decision and not documented:

```text
STOP → FLAG → ASK
```

# 100. Final Release Status

There are only two formal outputs:

```text
READY FOR PILOT
```

or:

```text
NOT READY FOR PILOT
```

The final status must be evidence-based.

If any BLOCKER remains:

```text
NOT READY FOR PILOT
```

# 101. What Comes After M17

M17 completes the approved MVP implementation plan.

Do **not** automatically create M18.

After M17, the next step is:

```text
PILOT
→ OBSERVE
→ COLLECT EVIDENCE
→ IDENTIFY PRODUCT GAPS
→ PRIORITIZE POST-PILOT BACKLOG
```

Any next implementation phase should be based on:

- pilot feedback,
- defects,
- usage patterns,
- curriculum needs,
- FICI product priorities.
